summary: Revise at 6.3. Caiman is 7.0 and the ship bar is 7.5; on the calibration scale this sits just under Corvus (6.6, cut). There were no earlier review rounds; this round also checks the three read-test-3 changes. Every gate recorded in report.json is green at draft (768x320) and at export (1536x448). The template gate is not recorded yet. The table is now a convincing Gothic seal matrix: a pointed, cusped quatrefoil, a mirrored minuscule Textura legend (sigillum capituli ecclesie cathedralis) with a cross pattee, and a fleur, inside a ruled band. The face view reads 'ecclesiastical seal' unprompted. Below the table, the ring is a bare factory 017 cushion signet. Five recessed lancets sit under each table edge, and in the hero they read as a row of notches or battlements rather than arches. The shoulder roundels render as melted blobs in palm and reverse. The shoulder windows are open line outlines whose straight sides stop short, so they look unfinished. Density from shoulder to palm is far below Caiman and the Reptilia signets. The fleur also carries a real defect. Its band is a slab that runs off the axis to the left, and below the band the foot and spikes are ghosted, smeared shapes. Because of this, the hero still reads 'knot / figure-eight' (read-test-3 change 1 is not met). The outer border is still 12 rounded foils (change 2 is not met). The arcade grew to 5 lancets at sink 0.45, but they are 2.0 to 2.8 mm tall, not the 3.2 asked for (change 3 is partly met). One concrete round can lift this to about 7.5: repair the fleur, sharpen the border, deepen the legend, and give the shoulders crisp, legible architecture.
strengths: The face (face.png, face-300.png) is a credible medieval seal matrix. It holds a pointed four-lobed quatrefoil with sharp cusps, a full-circle mirrored Textura legend with a cross pattee, and a ruled inner band. It is the best seal read this ring has had, and it fills the table edge to edge.
The seal is honestly bench-cut. Every table stamp is bench=true, and the cast stamps (arcade, roundels) are along_pull. The casting pattern is closed and leaves the seal out, as the concept asks.
The 017 fallback is well argued in stock_fallback_why: 005 domes 1.1 mm and fills 0.67 mm, while 017 fills 0.011 mm. The table's hard wall-to-face angle survives intact (bare-vs-finished.png).
In side.png the cheek arcade reads clearly as five pointed lancets. It is the best architectural passage below the table.
Metal is ample: 4.20 mm under the deepest 0.95 mm cut, and a thinnest wall of 1.46 mm.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: The face carries the theme fully. The cheeks carry a narrow lancet row, and the shoulders carry one open-outline window plus three small roundels each. The shank sides and palm are bare polish. The theme stops at about theta 35/145, so the lower two thirds of the ring say 'stock signet', not chapter house.

checklist.item: Reads as its Gothic subject at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: face-300 reads 'Gothic seal matrix', with the quatrefoil, the blackletter legend and the mirrored lettering. hero-300 is weaker. The fleur collapses into a knot, and the cheek lancets read as notches. Still, the cusped quatrefoil and the legend band carry the read. It is not a perforated or grooved band.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing/smearing/stair-steps
checklist.reason: There are three failures. (1) The fleur's lower half (stamps 'Seal fleur, band', 'foot', 'left/right spike'): the band renders as an off-centre slab extending about 1 mm left of the axis, and the foot and spikes beneath it are ghosted, smeared lobes with no clean edges (face.png, stones.png). (2) The shoulder roundels render as melted, blobby clusters in palm.png, reverse.png and shoulder.png; none shows four clean cusped foils. (3) The arcade lancet flanks show a sawtooth stair-step along the arch sides in side.png. The legend letters and the quatrefoil rules are crisp.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, à jour, coloured as stained glass
checklist.reason: Not applicable. The concept carries no stones; stones.json is empty and the preview shows 0.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: Below the table the ring is untouched stock polish with flat-floored recesses. The shoulder windows are single-line engraved outlines with open ends (reverse.png, shoulder.png), which read as unfinished CAD, not a sculpted window. The table work is good, but it is engraving and has no modelled form.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: bare-vs-finished.png and hero.png keep 017's crisp table-to-wall edge. Envelope fill is 0.011 mm.

checklist.item: Distinct silhouette; custom heads >= 13 mm; shoulder ornament not cut off before the face
checklist.reason: This is factory stock at 16 x 15.6 mm, so no custom head is needed and it clears 13 mm. The silhouette is the stock cushion signet, distinct among Tenebrae only by being the plain seal. The shoulder ornament runs up into the cheek arcade without a gap.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The face has medium (quatrefoil, fleur) and small (letters, cusps) forms, but no large modelled form anywhere. Against Caiman's hero, which is worked edge to edge on head, shoulders and shank, Sigillum's hero is about 60% bare polish. The Reptilia signets (Varanus on the same 017) are patterned to the palm.

gates.gate: Template gate (<= 4 design.set patches within class budget)
gates.verified: No verification.json and no template block in report.json. This gate is not yet run. It must be recorded before a ship verdict; design.ring.json is 957,141 bytes, inside the 1 MB stock budget.

punch_list.zone: Table centre: stamps 'Seal fleur, band', 'Seal fleur, foot', 'Seal fleur, left spike', 'Seal fleur, right spike' (theta 90, v 9.30)
punch_list.change: Rebuild the fleur's lower half. Centre the band on the fleur's axis; it now runs about 1 mm further left than right. Cut it as a clean bar about 3.6 x 0.8 mm at the same 0.85 depth, with no slab that reads proud. Redraw the foot as three closed lobes (centre about 1.4 mm tall, sides about 1.0 mm) and the spikes as closed outlines, each separated from the band and from the quatrefoil wall by at least 0.4 mm of uncut field. Grow the whole fleur from 5.0 to about 5.6 mm tall, and widen the centre petal by about 25%. This is read-test-3 change 1, still open.
punch_list.acceptance: face.png: band symmetric about the fleur's axis within 0.1 mm; the foot shows three crisp separate lobes with no ghosted or smeared outline. hero-300.png: a viewer names 'fleur-de-lis', not 'knot' or 'figure eight'.

punch_list.zone: Shoulders, theta 25-50 and 130-155: stamps 'Shoulder window, right/left' (bench) and 'Shoulder roundel 1/2' (cast, side faces)
punch_list.change: Replace the open single-line window with a closed two-light lancet window, about 5.0 x 3.0 mm. Cut the lights and oculus as recessed fields (sink 0.35, bench), with the mullion and tracery left proud at no less than 0.5 mm. Every outline must close; the straight sides now stop short of the sill. Redraw the shoulder roundels as four-foil cusped outlines with crisp edges, at Ø 2.4 / 2.0 / 1.6 (now 2.40 / 1.85 / 1.27), sink 0.35, along_pull. The melted look in palm and reverse comes from foil lobes merging at this size, so either open the foil gaps to at least 0.30 mm or drop to a single cusped circle.
punch_list.acceptance: shoulder.png and reverse.png: the window shows two pointed lights and an oculus inside a closed arch, and each roundel shows four separable foils. hero-300.png: at least one window and two roundels are visible on the near shoulder.

punch_list.zone: Shank side faces (±z walls), theta 0-30 and 150-180 on both sides, continuing from the shoulder roundels toward the palm
punch_list.change: Carry the chapter-house theme down the shank so the ring is not 60% bare stock. Add a cast blind arcade of 5 to 7 pointed lancets per side face, each about 1.6 x 1.0 mm, sink 0.30, along_pull, graded smaller toward the palm. Alternatively, continue the roundel chain at Ø 1.4 to 1.0. Keep the palm crown plain, as the concept says.
punch_list.acceptance: side.png and reverse.png: ornament runs continuously from the cheek arcade to within about 20 deg of the palm. hero.png: no polished field larger than about 4 x 4 mm on the near shank side.

punch_list.zone: Table rim: stamps 'Cusped border, foil 1-12' (r about 7.2 mm)
punch_list.change: Turn the 12 rounded foils into pointed Gothic cusping. Draw arcs that meet at sharp inward points, cusp depth about 0.6 mm, and redraw the points so they are visible at 300 px. This is read-test-3 change 2, still open.
punch_list.acceptance: face-300.png: the rim shows 12 countable sharp points and no longer reads as a coin, rosette or bottle-cap edge.

punch_list.change: Deepen the legend from 0.10 to 0.35-0.40 mm, as the concept specifies (-0.40), and the border and quatrefoil rules to 0.25-0.30 mm. A 0.10 mm intaglio makes a faint wax impression, and it washes out in the hero highlight (the upper-right letters of 'cathedralis' are lost in hero.png). Metal allows it: 4.20 mm stands under the deepest cut.
punch_list.acceptance: hero.png: every letter of the legend arc shows a dark floor, including the upper right in the highlight. face-300.png: the legend reads as a dark band, not a pale ring.

punch_list.zone: Cheeks ±z under the table: stamps 'Chapter-house arcade 1/2, 1-5' (theta 71-109)
punch_list.change: Raise the lancets from 2.0-2.8 to about 3.2 mm, filling the cheek height. Keep the equilateral pointed heads and sink 0.45, along_pull. Smooth the arch flanks, which now show a sawtooth stair-step in side.png: raise the stamp outline resolution or the build resolution on this stamp so each flank is one clean curve.
punch_list.acceptance: hero-300.png: the near cheek shows pointed arches (heads countable), not notches or battlements. side.png: arch flanks are smooth curves with no visible steps.

punch_list.change: Run the template gate, then record its patch count, its size and the per-phase open time in verification.json.
punch_list.acceptance: verification.json shows at most 4 design.set patches, a byte-identical cold evaluation with the same mesh, and size within the stock budget (1 MB).

punch_list.zone: Release study: sand slot at [6.73, 7.98, 4.04] and the export note on negative-draft faces (worst draft -0.41 deg)
punch_list.change: Find which feature makes the 0.20 mm sand slot (likely a roundel or arcade edge, z = 4.04 on the +x side) and widen it to at least 0.30 mm, the Delft detail. Check the negative-draft faces at 0.05 mm sampling.
punch_list.acceptance: release_0100_sand_findings lists no slot under 0.30 mm, and the export release notes no longer report unresolved negative-draft faces, or name them as stock or bore.
